questions.question: Why should you keep an adequate distance behind other vehicles?

options.text: To give yourself time and space to see and react to hazards.
So you can tailgate.
To help traffic counters count vehicles accurately.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give yourself time and space to see and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A good following distance lets you stop or swerve if the car ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see hazards on the road, like potholes.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier because you can see the lights of other vehicles.
Harder because it is more difficult to see.
Not allowed on highways.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder because it is more difficult to see.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because you cannot see as well. Without normal light and shadows, it is harder to judge how far away things are.

questions.question: Studies show that when motorcycles have their headlights on during the day:

options.text: They are not as easy to see as other vehicles.
Other drivers notice them more than when the headlight is off.
Other drivers get confused.
They are less safe than when the headlight is off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers notice them more than when the headlight is off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on when you ride. A motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers during the day.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Twice a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This takes only a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you ride.

questions.question: What should proper motorcycle riding clothes cover?

options.text: Your arms and legs completely.
Your arms completely, but your legs can be exposed.
Your legs completely, but your arms can be exposed.
Whatever feels most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely for protection while riding.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: Your feet can touch the ground while you are sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet can touch the ground while you are sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you if your feet reach the ground when you sit on it. You should also be able to reach and operate the controls easily.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?

options.text: Time
Coffee
Exercise
Fresh air

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time reduces the effects of alcohol. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers may keep you awake, but they do not reduce alcohol in your body.

questions.question: When must you wear a helmet?

options.text: All motorcycle operators must wear one.
Operators under 18 must wear one.
Operators who have not had their license for two years must wear one.
Helmets are never required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Operators under 18 must wear one.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders under 18 and riders on a motorcycle permit must wear an approved helmet. All riders should wear a helmet every time they ride.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Ignore them.
Change lanes safely and let them pass.
Speed up.
Leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes safely and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to move them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate faster.

questions.question: Which surface would be slippery for a motorcycle?

options.text: Wet pavement
A driveway
Dry pavement
A parking lot

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are slippery surfaces. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: Which surface provides good traction?

options.text: Wet pavement
Dry pavement
Lane markings
Snow

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings are all slippery. Dry pavement is the safest surface for a motorcycle.

questions.question: What footwear is best for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Sturdy boots
Tennis shoes
Shoes with loose laces
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles. High-top boots or heavy shoes work well. If your laces are long, tuck them in before riding so they do not get caught.

questions.question: When riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good riding condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
Ride as you usually do, since most bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding, get familiar with the new bike. Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times to learn how they feel.

questions.question: When operating a motorcycle, what must you do with your license?

options.text: You do not need to carry your license with you.
You must carry your license with you.
Your license must be affixed to your helmet.
Your license must be affixed to your right arm.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must carry your license with you.
questions.explanation: You must carry your valid driver license with a motorcycle endorsement every time you ride. If you have a learner's permit, carry that with you on every ride too.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Stay where you are to avoid surprising the driver.
Wave at the other driver to get their attention.
Slow down until you are out of the blind spot.
Pull over to the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down until you are out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, either speed up quickly or slow down to get out of it. Do not stay in the blind spot.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must have:

options.text: A seat that is large enough for two riders.
Only one set of footrests.
A passenger who does not wear protective clothing.
A sticker on the brake light to warn other motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle has a seat for two. The bike must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you wear.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car, what is likely true?

options.text: You are likely riding in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
The driver will most likely know you are there.
You are discouraging other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car. This way the driver will see you in their rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Sit with your arms propping you up rather than steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Allow your feet to hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to help with balance in turns. Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent at the handgrips. Use your arms to steer, not to support your weight. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: For the best protection, a helmet should:

options.text: Have a few cracks.
Not be certified.
Have frayed straps.
Fit snugly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What is the single most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the most effective thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean with you as you lean.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with you as you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with the operator. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:

options.text: Leather.
Wool.
Polyester.
Silk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another durable material to protect your hands.

questions.question: An approved helmet should:

options.text: Let you see clearly to the sides as needed.
Restrict your side vision.
Usually be uncomfortable.
Have no markings or labels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let you see clearly to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels and markings with the manufacturer's name, instructions, and safety standard information.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of having an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend into traffic so other drivers don't notice you.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other road users. Use your turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space between you and other vehicles, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to act if dangers appear.

questions.question: You can become more visible by:

options.text: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
Not using your turn signal.
Wearing dark clothing.
Waving at people.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright or reflective clothing. Add extra lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed. These actions help other drivers notice you.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet for the most protection, pick one that:

options.text: Fits loosely.
Meets U.S. DOT standards.
Has been in a previous crash.
Provides hearing protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the best protection. A helmet should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: One benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is:

options.text: Your motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance is very costly.
Maintenance checks help prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle will keep running like new if you maintain it properly and do regular inspections as part of your maintenance routine.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Drag your feet on the ground.
Point your toes downward.
Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
Keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: For balance, place your feet firmly on the footrests. Do not drag them on the ground. Do not point your toes down, as this may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stay in the same position in the lane all the time.
Constantly move between lane positions to keep other drivers out.
Pick a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about where they are in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pick a lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may be going slowly while looking for parking.
The road may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Parked cars create several dangers. A driver may pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.
